title: Security concerns: Delhi Police denies permission for Diljit Dosanjh's Oct 30 concert
content: The excitement for Diljit Dosanjh’s concert in Delhi has been dashed after the police denied permission for the event at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. Fans are left disappointed as the festive season approaches, with security concerns and law and order issues influencing this decision. Organizers are now faced with the challenge of possibly seeking new permits or rescheduling the concert, marking a setback for the Aura India Tour.

title: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean
content: President Trump has recently proposed renaming the Atlantic Ocean, following prior discussions about the Atlantic Ocean. During a recent event, he mentioned contacting Google Maps regarding these renaming efforts. Google CEO Sundar Pichai reportedly declined his proposal on the grounds that oceans encompass multiple countries. This follows the US administration's earlier renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users.

title: New York court overturns foreclosure sale order in $400,000 mortgage row
content: A recent ruling by an appeals court has overturned a foreclosure decision related to a property in Babylon, New York. The court determined that Bank of America did not give the borrower adequate notice prior to starting foreclosure procedures and failed to show that it had the necessary standing in the case. Consequently, the court rejected the bank's request for a summary judgment against the estate of Alice McNamara.

title: Rogue AI? US banks sound alarm over unauthorised access by 'agents'
content: Top US banks, including Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan Chase, are implementing restrictions on third-party AI access amid security worries. These institutions fear that unverified AI agents could potentially gain unauthorized access to customer accounts and conduct transactions autonomously. Some banks are open to allowing read-only permissions, but they remain vigilant against possible financial risks.

title: Florida girl named in sperm donor's will loses claim to his house
content: A Florida appeals court has upheld the rejection of a young girl's claim to a deceased man's house, despite his having named her in his will. The dispute involved a 2017 sperm donor agreement between Melissa Azrack and Malcolm Dorman. The appeal failed because Azrack did not challenge the lower court's finding that the property was not protected homestead property.

title: Sofía Vergara's Beverly Hills villa listed for $19.6m, sold for $13.7m
content: Sofía Vergara has officially sold her stunning Tuscan-style estate in Beverly Hills for $13.7 million in April 2024. Initially listed at $19.6 million in July 2022, after significant renovations, the price was reduced. Vergara, who acquired the property in 2014 for $10.6 million with Joe Manganiello, achieved a $3.1 million profit before expenses, boasting seven bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, and luxurious amenities throughout.

title: Rare 1896 Chaucer book with 87 woodcuts sold for Rs 2.68 crore
content: A stunning 1896 edition of 'The Works of Geoffrey Chaucer' has recently fetched around Rs 2.68 crore at auction. Known as the Kelmscott Chaucer, this edition showcases exquisite craftsmanship and features the original white pigskin binding crafted by William Morris. With only about 50 deluxe copies ever bound, this book's rarity and artistic illustrations by Edward Burne-Jones continue to captivate collectors, emphasizing the allure of beautifully crafted literary works.

title: United Airlines CEO says Starlink is helping win customers; Musk responds
content: This week, United Airlines aims to have Starlink on more than half of its flights, looking to fully implement the service across its fleet by the end of the following year. CEO Scott Kirby believes this partnership offers a distinct edge in attracting new passengers, especially as rising fuel costs weigh on profits amidst ongoing geopolitical issues.

title: Why some people struggle to say no even when exhausted, according to psychology
content: Saying yes to others' requests can be a common pattern for people-pleasers, leading to stress and overcommitment. This habit stems from a fear of disappointing others, which can make saying no feel uncomfortable. Continued agreement may cause emotional exhaustion and hinder personal relationships. Effective strategies for setting boundaries include pausing before answering requests and practicing refusal in low-pressure situations.

title: In a first, Australia's Ghost Shark submarine turns into aerial drone launchpad
content: Australia's Ghost Shark submarine has impressively demonstrated its ability to launch aerial drones for military applications. Capable of deploying various payloads, from sea mines to logistical support, this platform significantly enhances operational flexibility. Defence Industry Minister Pat Conroy emphasized that the initiative is designed to refine autonomous underwater combat strategies, with advanced communication systems ensuring smooth coordination of drone operations.

title: Virginia teen's model improves simulated earthquake sensor coverage by 16.7%
content: A 14-year-old student from Williamsburg, Virginia, has become one of 30 finalists in a national science competition after developing a mathematical model to improve earthquake sensor placement. Isabel Rossi's six-month research project showed that adding just five sensors could increase simulated detection coverage by 16.7%. She used earthquake records from California and mathematical methods to identify better sensor locations.

title: Shamonda virus detected in human for first time in France; patient dies
content: French health authorities reported the emergence of the Shamonda virus in a human for the first time. This case involved a severely immunocompromised patient who tragically passed away in Lyon. Investigations suggest the virus was contracted through an insect bite, likely from the Culicoides midge. Although the Shamonda virus has been prevalent in livestock, no general health risk has currently been identified.

title: Facial laser session leaves woman with burns; consumer panel orders Rs 1.11 lakh payout
content: In an alarming incident at Berkowits Hair & Skin Clinic in Bengaluru, a woman suffered severe second-degree burns during a laser hair removal treatment. Despite her intense pain, the technician minimized her discomfort, labeling it as normal. Subsequent medical examinations validated her injuries. The district consumer commission held the clinic accountable for inadequate service and mandated compensation, including a refund and damages for her injuries and emotional distress.

title: ‘Rahul Gandhi, Raihan Vadra’: BJP takes 'launch' jibe as photo exhibition row escalates
content: Political tensions have escalated following the removal of photographs from Raihan Vadra's exhibition at Bikaner House. BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia criticized the Gandhi family for allegedly promoting Raihan for political ambitions. Raihan Vadra expressed concerns about censorship and the impact on artistic expression following the objections from the venue management. Both Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Robert Vadra have expressed their support for Raihan in this matter.

title: US soldier killed at 17 in Korean War identified after 75 years, to be buried
content: Pvt. Joseph E. Boyd, who went missing in action at just 17 during the Korean War, has finally been identified decades later. His remains, previously known as Unknown X-1642, have been matched to his identity through advanced forensic techniques, including DNA testing. A dignified burial ceremony is set for October 21, 2026, in Owings Mills, Maryland, underscoring the ongoing commitment to honor missing service members from historical conflicts.

title: Texas man, 86, spends 39 years building 62-foot boat; strangers step in
content: An 86-year-old man from Mineral Wells, Texas, has been building a 62-foot steel boat since 1987. After three visitors discovered his ambition, they launched a crowdfunding campaign to support the project. More than $41,000 has been raised towards completing the boat and moving it to a launch site. The remaining work on the vessel is expected to require about $50,000 in funding.

title: Meta Q3 results: Net income jumps 264% to $9.86 bn, but legal charge limit profits
content: Meta Platforms reported a net income of $9.86 billion in Q3 2026, tripling from the previous year. Overall revenue increased to $64.60 billion, primarily driven by higher advertising earnings. However, operating income declined due to a significant legal charge linked to teen mental health litigation. The company plans to invest heavily in artificial intelligence infrastructure to support future revenue growth.

title: Paid Rs 1 lakh for gold chain, got nothing; jeweller ordered to pay Rs 1.3 lakh
content: Himachal Pradesh state consumer commission upheld a decision directing Shri Ganesh Jewellers to refund Rs 1 lakh. Customer M R Chauhan made an advance payment for a gold chain that was never delivered. Despite repeated requests and a police complaint, the jeweller failed to return the money. The commission awarded compensation of Rs 20,000 for mental harassment and Rs 10,000 for litigation costs.

title: Viral fever, vomiting: How Praveen Kumar fought back to win Asian Para Games gold
content: Praveen Kumar won the men’s high jump T44/64 gold medal at the Asian Para Games in Japan. He accomplished this while dealing with a hip injury and battling fever, cold, and cough. Despite these challenges, he cleared 2.05m, setting a new Games record. His previous record was 1.95m in the T44 category. Praveen aims to defend his Paralympic title at the next Los Angeles Games.

title: 'Beacon of hope': Polish PM Tusk hails ties with India, calls PM Modi a 'friend'
content: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk visited India to strengthen bilateral cooperation between India and Poland. He highlighted the absence of conflicts of interest and shared values between the two nations. Both leaders discussed expanding economic opportunities through the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement. Tusk emphasized the positive economic developments achieved by Poland and India over the last 35 years.

title: Exhibition row: Raihan recounts how events unfolded before photos were taken down
content: Raihan Vadra's photography exhibition, No Idea Is Fine, allegedly faced turmoil at Bikaner House when management objected hours before its start, claiming venue policy violations. While Vadra proposed removing select images, the officials demanded the removal of all 70 photographs, including those depicting the Indian national flag. This sparked outrage among Congress members, igniting debates about censorship and the value of artistic freedom.

title: Pala-era Vishnu sculpture sold for Rs 8.16 crore, over 9 times estimate
content: A blackstone sculpture of Vishnu, dating to the 11th or 12th century, sold for £635,000 at Christie’s auction. The sculpture was previously part of a Swiss collection and first sold in March 1973. Over the years, the artwork maintained its significance and desirability among collectors. In June 2026, it was auctioned again as part of a collection focusing on South Asian art.

title: China's restored reefs hold 286 oysters per sq m; particles down 62%
content: A study of oyster reef restoration in China's Bohai Bay has found encouraging signs of marine habitat recovery between 2022 and 2026. By March 2026, artificial reefs supported an average of 286 oysters per square metre, while suspended particles in the water had declined by approximately 62%. Published in Frontiers in Marine Science, the study also recorded an increase in seabed animals. However, researchers said further monitoring was needed to establish the project's long-term effectiveness.

title: Georgia woman loses marijuana smoke case as court upholds pension fund immunity
content: A Georgia woman sued after claiming her neighbour’s marijuana smoke repeatedly entered her apartment despite a no-smoking lease, affecting her breathing and health. Bridget Francis alleged that the apartment management ignored her complaints. However, on October 19, 2026, a Georgia appeals court upheld the dismissal of her claims against a California teachers’ pension fund, ruling that it was legally protected from the lawsuit.

title: Delhi-NCR pollution: How GRAP Stage 1 curbs can protect your heart and lungs
content: Delhi-NCR has launched GRAP Stage 1 to combat the rising air pollution levels and protect health standards. The initiative focuses on controlling dust, limiting specific fuel types, and tightening regulatory enforcement. Health experts stress the importance of immediate intervention to guard vulnerable populations against the health implications of poor air quality. Citizens are urged to adopt personal safety measures during smoggy days.

title: 'Vidhan Sabha uda diya': Bengaluru police arrest Bihar man over AI video
content: Bengaluru City Police have arrested a 25-year-old migrant worker for posting an alarming AI-generated video online. The video depicted a bomb blast at Vidhana Soudha, the Karnataka government's seat. The suspect, Hazrat Ali Shoiab, had been working as a daily-wage pipefitter in the city. Police discovered the footage during routine digital surveillance and tracked down the suspect's account. Investigations are ongoing to understand Shoiab's motives and identify any collaborators.

title: ‘It was scripted, a joke’: Delhi influencer apologises over racial abuse of Tripura youth
content: Facing significant backlash, social media influencer Amir Shokeen publicly apologized for a racially abusive video. Directed towards the people of Tripura and its chief minister, his apology sought to address the hurt caused. The incident has sparked an investigation by the Delhi Police's IFSO unit, prompted by complaints from the Tripura Students Forum Delhi, with political leaders Kiren Rijiju and Manik Saha calling for legal action.

title: Sheetal Devi strikes double gold again! Repeats 2023 Asian Para Games feat in 2026
content: Indian para-archer Sheetal Devi achieved remarkable success by winning two gold medals at the Asian Para Games. She defended her individual title by defeating Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah in a tight match. Earlier, Sheetal partnered with Toman Kumar to secure gold in the mixed team event. She also won a silver medal in women's compound doubles alongside Payal Nag.

title: Tiger Shroff firing: Accused practised shooting near Mumbai, bullet hit hotel bed
content: Following the alarming shooting incident involving Tiger Shroff, authorities have apprehended multiple suspects. Investigations revealed a nearby location in Mumbai where these individuals honed their shooting skills. The police are now exploring potential ties between the arrested parties and the incident itself. Furthermore, an audio recording containing a threatening message aimed at Shroff is set to undergo voice verification analysis as part of this thorough investigation.

title: Pompeii's grandest house gets €1.4m restoration paid for by private donor
content: Thanks to a private sponsor, the House of Marcus Fabius Rufus in Pompeii is set for restoration, with a portion expected to welcome guided groups by this Christmas. The renovation focuses on fresco restoration and improved visitor access, addressing the extensive damage the site suffered since its closure in 1980 due to a volcanic eruption.

title: Was Tiger Shroff the real target? | Pulse Maharashtra
content:
A celebrity shootout in Mumbai has sent shockwaves through the financial capital and has spread fear in the Hindi film industry. This wasn’t the first shootout in the city this year. And now, the industry is scared of the dark shadows of the past, when the underworld called the shots in Bollywood. And just like the past, this time too, the masterminds seem to be operating from foreign shores. But was Tiger Shroff the real target? Is this shootout related to incidents like the firing outside actor Salman Khan’s residence, the murder of NCP leader Baba Siddique, the shooting outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty’s residence and the reported threats to actors Ranveer Singh and Aamir Khan?

In this week’s Pulse Maharashtra with Vinaya Deshpande, we take you through what we know so far and what the unanswered questions are. And how this attack leads to an old fear in the heart of an industry which is one of India’s greatest soft powers in the world – Bollywood.

title: CJP leaders released after court rejects police plea for extended custody
content:

The court eventually ordered their release after they submitted undertakings promising not to organise protests at Jantar Mantar while the site remains denotified and not to disturb public peace.

content: the remarks came as Trump campaigned for Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley in north Carolina . despite campaigning for a candidate in another state, Trump returned to talking about Hutchinson . "it's not my thing. Nothing wrong with it, of course. But it's never been my thing," he said .

title: 'Congress spreading anarchy': BJP draws parallel between France and Delhi protests
content: BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia repeatedly referred to Gandhi as “Rahul Gaddar” . he alleged that the Congress leadership’s engagement with international groups raised questions about their activities, funding and possible coordination with protests in India . his remarks followed a Fox News Digital investigation that claimed to have identified 101 organisations across nine countries involved in organising, coordinating or amplifying demonstrations .

title: Russia targets European firms, largely spares US businesses as Putin-Trump ties warm
content: only three of the 20 foreign-owned companies under Russian administration were linked to the us . the remaining companies were controlled by European firms . a person close to Russian financial regulators told news agency Reuters that Moscow had little incentive to adopt the same hard line towards US firms as it had towards European businesses .

title: ‘Glaring inaccuracies’: New Delhi rebukes UN over ‘India-based’ tag for Dawood’s D-Company
content: fugitive gangster dawood Ibrahim is leader of "India-based" criminal gang . india has pushed back against a UN special rapporteur for bias in a counter-terror report . it flagged "glaring inaccuracies" in the counter-terrorism report, a report says . a u.n. special report on the promotion and protection of human rights .

title: ‘Anti-Indian hate is exploding’: US lawmaker Raja Krishnamoorthi blames big tech firms
content: Indian-origin US Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi has accused major technology companies of benefiting from anti-Indian, anti-Hindu and anti-South Asian hatred on social media . his remarks follow a report by the Center for the Study of Organized Hate (CSOH), which documented a rise in online hostility towards south Asian communities in the united states .

title: Houthis claim Saudi Arabia targeted boat carrying 14 Indians; launch rescue ops
content: the houthi rebels claim they are attempting to rescue a boat carrying 14 Indians . they claim the boat was targeted by what they described as the 'Saudi enemy' the vessel was carrying 14 indian nationals near Zuqar Island in the red sea .

title: Lincoln's signed photo found in old desk later sold for $149,020
content: the signed portrait of Abraham Lincoln sold at auction for $149,020 . the portrait was taken on February 9, 1864, by Anthony Berger at mathew Brady's photographic studio in washington . it was taken by a former newspaper clipping that helped establish its remarkable history .

title: CJP leaders seek more time to appear before Delhi Police crime branch
content: police are expected to issue a fresh notice to the two leaders, sources say . the two were released after a special executive magistrate court accepted their personal and surety bonds . they were also instructed to appear on every hearing date and comply with the conditions specified in their bonds and undertakings .
